parts.title: Paper vs Fabric: We Hung Weights Until One TORE! (Part 1) | Strength
parts.description:
Paper or fabric: which one tears first? We hang weights on both, one at a time, until one TEARS! Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: strong vs flexible.

In this part:
• What is a physical property? Something we can measure or observe (look closer)
• The pull test: weights on a paper strip and a fabric strip, until one tears (look closer, in slow motion)
• Be a thread: inside a school bag's fabric
• Strength: strong or fragile?
• HOLD ON! The drop test: a metal cup and a glass cup (look closer; an adult does this test)
• Spot the hidden spider!

Key words: physical property, strength, strong, fragile.
Watch Part 2: rubber band vs ice-cream stick, which one snaps? Last episode: what are things made of? The 7 materials.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity of materials: physical properties, strength and flexibility (Chapter 3, pp. 53–55). Also fits US NGSS 2-PS1-1 (Grade 2 to 3).
Safety: never break, drop or snap things to test them. In this video an adult does the tests, safely. At home, just look and gently feel.
Try it at home: find one flexible thing and one rigid thing in your room and show someone at home. Do not bend the rigid one!
Singapore and the US: the rubber band round your packet of chicken rice is flexible. The plastic ruler in your pencil case bends a little; a wooden one hardly bends. In the US (Grade 2 to 3): a paper grocery bag can tear under heavy cans, and you test materials the same way: change one thing, keep the rest the same.

parts.title: Rubber Band vs Ice-Cream Stick: Which One SNAPS? (Part 2) | Flexibility
parts.description:
A rubber band and an ice-cream stick. Bend them both. Which one SNAPS? Be a rubber band and find out! Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: strong vs flexible.

In this part:
• The bend test: a rubber band and an ice-cream stick (look closer)
• Flexibility: flexible or rigid?
• Be a rubber band: round a packet of chicken rice
• Three tubes: rubber, plastic, metal. Which is the most flexible? (look closer)
• Showdown: find the mistake in Momo's notes
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden caterpillar!

Key words: flexibility, flexible, rigid.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: a metal spoon sinks, so how does a giant metal ship float?
